requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'Verbalizable Representations Form a Global Workspace in Language Models' have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: The compute environment, target language models (Claude Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5, and optionally Opus 4.6, plus any open-source models used for cross-validation), tokenizers, and residual-stream access APIs required to compute Jacobians and perform activation interventions are available and correctly configured.
Target Anthropic Claude models required for the paper's core experiments are accessible with residual-stream and gradient introspection capabilities.
Code has been implemented that loads Claude Sonnet 4.5 as the default model for all experiments, with access to per-layer residual-stream activations at every token position.

verification.spec: Import the project's model loader and instantiate the default model. Assert that (a) the loaded model identifier/config corresponds to Claude Sonnet 4.5 (or a documented open-weight substitute if API access is unavailable), and (b) a hook or forward-pass API exposes per-layer residual-stream tensors of shape [batch, seq_len, d_model] at every layer index for a short test prompt. Verify residual streams are retrievable at all token positions by checking tensor shapes match seq_len of the tokenized prompt.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that loads Claude Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5 as corroboration models for key experiments (verbal report, internal reasoning, directed modulation), with the same residual-stream access as Sonnet 4.5.

verification.spec: Import the model loader with model identifiers for Haiku 4.5 and Opus 4.5 (or documented substitutes). For each, instantiate the model and verify that the same residual-stream access API used for Sonnet 4.5 returns per-layer activations of shape [batch, seq_len, d_model] on a short test prompt. Assert both models are loadable via the same interface.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that optionally loads Claude Opus 4.6 for the multi-step arithmetic and additional analyses described in the paper.

verification.spec: Instantiate a Claude Opus 4.6 handle (or documented substitute) via the model-loading interface and verify a short forward pass succeeds and residual-stream activations can be extracted at every layer.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that loads an open-source language model (e.g., a model available on Neuronpedia) for cross-validation of J-lens findings.

verification.spec: Load an open-source LLM (e.g., Llama-3.1-8B) via the project's loader. Verify the model can be instantiated on the available hardware, that per-layer residual-stream activations are accessible via hooks, and that the unembedding matrix W_U is retrievable as a tensor attribute. Run a short forward pass on a test prompt and confirm output logits shape [batch, seq_len, vocab_size].

sub_tasks.requirements: Model internals required by the Jacobian lens methodology are exposed for read and write operations.
Code has been implemented that provides access to the residual stream h_ℓ at every transformer layer ℓ and every token position t during a forward pass.

verification.spec: Run a forward pass on a prompt of length T and confirm the API returns h_ℓ with shape [T, d_model] for every layer ℓ in [0, n_layers). Then, using the accessor at (ℓ, t), verify that adding a small perturbation and re-running produces final logits that change (i.e., accessor is hooked into the live computation, not a detached copy).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that exposes the unembedding matrix W_U and any final-layer normalization operations so that logits can be computed from arbitrary residual-stream vectors.

verification.spec: Import the model wrapper and confirm it exposes W_U (unembedding matrix) and any final-layer normalization (e.g., final layer norm). Multiply W_U by a random residual-stream vector of shape (d_model,) after applying the normalization and confirm output shape is (vocab_size,).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports backpropagation from the final-layer residual stream h_final,t' back to an intermediate residual stream h_ℓ,t to compute the Jacobian ∂h_final,t'/∂h_ℓ,t.

verification.spec: Run a forward pass on a short prompt, select an intermediate layer ℓ and positions t, t'. Compute the Jacobian J = ∂h_final,t'/∂h_ℓ,t via autograd (backpropagating one column at a time or with jacrev). Verify J has shape [d_model, d_model] and that J @ δ approximates the change in h_final,t' induced by perturbing h_ℓ,t by a small δ (finite-difference agreement within 1e-3 relative error).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that supports activation patching / write interventions: at specified (layer, position) locations the residual stream can be replaced or additively modified during a forward pass, with the modified pass continuing normally.

verification.spec: Register a write-side hook at (layer ℓ, position t). Perform a clean forward pass recording logits L_clean. Then rerun with the hook that replaces h_ℓ,t with h_ℓ,t + α v for a known direction v; verify subsequent layers see the modified value (final logits differ from L_clean) and that the change matches the linearized prediction Jαv within tolerance for small α.

sub_tasks.requirements: Tokenizer and layer-indexing conventions used throughout the paper are implemented consistently.

Code has been implemented that loads the tokenizer corresponding to each Claude model and exposes vocabulary size d_vocab and per-token strings so J-lens readouts can be rendered as human-readable tokens.

verification.spec: Load the tokenizer for the configured model and confirm vocab_size matches the model's unembedding matrix row count. Confirm token-id -> string decoding works by decoding token id 0 and a few sample ids to human-readable strings.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that reindexes the model's residual-stream layers onto 25 evenly spaced layers scaled to the range [0, 100] so that reported layer numbers are interpretable as percentages of depth.

verification.spec: Call the project's layer-reindexing utility for the loaded model. Assert it returns exactly 25 layer indices, that the mapped values are evenly spaced in [0, 100] (e.g., 0, ~4.17, ..., 100), and that each index corresponds to a valid layer in the underlying model. Verify by checking that layer_indices has length 25 and np.diff(scaled_layers) has near-constant spacing (std < 0.1).

sub_tasks.requirements: Compute infrastructure and numerical settings are configured to support Jacobian computation at the scale required by the paper.

Code has been implemented that allocates GPU (or equivalent accelerator) resources sufficient to hold Sonnet 4.5-scale models and to backpropagate d_model × d_model Jacobians from final-layer positions to intermediate layers.

verification.spec: Query torch.cuda for available devices and total memory. Assert at least one accelerator is present with >=40GB memory. Then, load the target model and successfully execute a backward pass from a final-layer residual-stream position to an intermediate-layer residual stream using torch.autograd.functional.jacobian or manual jvp/vjp, producing a d_model x d_model Jacobian tensor without OOM.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that sets the numerical precision (e.g., bf16/fp32) and any deterministic-mode flags so that Jacobian computations and downstream interventions are reproducible across runs.

verification.spec: Import the config/setup module and confirm it explicitly sets numerical precision (e.g., torch.set_default_dtype or a bf16/fp32 config flag) and any determinism flags (torch.use_deterministic_algorithms or seed-setting). Assert the config exposes named precision and determinism fields.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that fixes random seeds for prompt sampling, decoding, and any stochastic intervention procedures to make the reported experiments reproducible.

verification.spec: Call the seeding utility with a fixed seed, then run prompt sampling and a stochastic decoding pass twice. Confirm outputs are identical bitwise across the two runs, demonstrating that random seeds control prompt sampling, decoding, and intervention procedures.

sub_tasks.requirements: Setup is validated end-to-end so that Jacobian computation and intervention APIs behave correctly before being used in downstream experiments.

Code has been implemented that provides a smoke test verifying that a single forward pass on a short prompt returns a residual-stream tensor of shape (n_layers, n_tokens, d_model) for each configured model.

verification.spec: Run a forward pass on a short prompt (e.g., 'Hello world') with output_hidden_states enabled and assert the returned residual-stream tensor has shape (n_layers, n_tokens, d_model) for the configured model.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that verifies gradients can flow from the final-layer residual stream at a chosen position back to an intermediate residual stream, producing a finite non-zero Jacobian matrix as a sanity check.

verification.spec: Enable gradient computation, run a forward pass, and backpropagate from a single element of the final-layer residual stream to an intermediate residual stream at some layer ℓ. Assert the resulting Jacobian tensor is finite (torch.isfinite all True) and contains nonzero entries.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that verifies an activation-patching write intervention modifies the model's next-token distribution on a controlled test prompt (e.g., zeroing out the final-layer residual stream produces a degenerate/random output distribution).

verification.spec: Run a forward pass on a test prompt and record baseline next-token logits. Then hook the final-layer residual stream and zero it out, rerun the forward pass, and confirm the resulting next-token distribution differs substantially (e.g., KL divergence > 1.0 or top-1 token changes) from baseline.

sub_tasks.requirements: Baseline lenses (logit lens, tuned lens, and Hernandez-style relation Jacobians) are implemented for systematic comparison against the J-lens.
The logit lens baseline is implemented as J_ell = I (identity), applying WU and normalization directly to intermediate residual stream activations to produce per-layer vocabulary readouts.

Code has been implemented that applies the model's unembedding matrix WU (with the appropriate normalization used at the final layer) directly to residual stream activations h_ell at any layer, returning a score/logit vector over the full vocabulary.

verification.spec: Implement logit_lens(h_ℓ) = softmax(W_U @ norm(h_ℓ)) using the model's own final-layer norm (RMSNorm/LayerNorm parameters). Verify (a) output shape [vocab_size] with rows summing to 1, (b) at the final layer, logit_lens matches the model's actual next-token distribution to within 1e-4 KL divergence, and (c) it can be applied at every intermediate layer without error.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that produces a ranked list of top-k vocabulary tokens from the logit lens readout at a given (layer, token position) matching the API used for J-lens readouts, so the two lenses can be compared on identical inputs.

verification.spec: Import the logit lens readout function. Verify (a) it applies W_U (with any norm) directly to intermediate residual stream, i.e., corresponds to J_ell = I; (b) its API signature matches the J-lens readout (accepting layer, position, top_k) and returns top-k token/score pairs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The logit lens produces interpretable/agreeing readouts with the J-lens in the final several layers and degrades in earlier layers, matching the paper's qualitative claim that the two lenses agree closely in late layers and diverge in early layers.

verification.spec: On a set of ~50 prompts, compute logit-lens and J-lens top-10 token lists at every layer. Compute the top-10 overlap (Jaccard) between the two lenses at each layer. Verify that the mean overlap in the last ~20% of layers is high (≥ 0.5) and that it monotonically decreases toward earlier layers, dropping to near-random overlap in the first 30% of layers.

sub_tasks.requirements: The tuned lens baseline is implemented, fitting per-layer linear (affine) maps trained to match the model's final output distribution from intermediate residual stream activations.
Code has been implemented that defines a per-layer affine transformation (weight matrix plus bias) mapping residual stream activations at layer ell into the final-layer residual stream space.

verification.spec: Import the tuned lens module. Confirm it defines a per-layer affine transformation (a weight matrix of shape [d_model, d_model] and a bias vector of shape [d_model]) for each intermediate layer, and that forward(x, layer) returns W_layer @ x + b_layer with output shape matching final-layer residual stream.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that trains each per-layer tuned lens map by minimizing a divergence (e.g., KL) between the tuned lens output distribution and the model's true final-layer next-token distribution over a training corpus.

verification.spec: For each layer ℓ, initialize a learnable affine map A_ℓ (d_model × d_model plus bias) and train it by minimizing KL(softmax(W_U @ norm(model_next_token_distribution)) || softmax(W_U @ norm(A_ℓ @ h_ℓ))) on a training corpus of ≥ 1000 sequences. Verify (a) training loss decreases across steps, (b) at convergence tuned-lens KL to the true final distribution is lower than logit-lens KL at the same layers, and (c) A_ℓ is saved per-layer.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies the trained tuned lens to any intermediate residual stream activation to produce a ranked list of vocabulary tokens, using the same readout interface as the logit lens and J-lens.

verification.spec: Import the tuned lens readout. Verify (a) it applies the per-layer affine transform then unembed to produce vocab-space logits; (b) it returns a ranked list of top-k tokens with the same API/shape as the logit and J-lens readouts.

sub_tasks.requirements: On prompts involving unverbalized intermediate computation (e.g., two-hop factual or arithmetic prompts), tuned lens readouts at intermediate layers tend to surface the final output token rather than the intermediate concept, reproducing the paper's 'skip ahead' observation.

verification.spec: On the two-hop intermediate-computation prompts of §3.3 (e.g., 'The number of legs on the animal that spins webs is'), compute tuned-lens top-5 tokens at every intermediate layer. Verify that in the majority of prompts, the final answer token (e.g., '8') appears in the tuned-lens top-5 across most intermediate layers, whereas the intermediate concept token (e.g., 'spider') rarely does, reproducing the 'skip-ahead' behavior.

sub_tasks.requirements: Hernandez-style per-relation Jacobian linear maps are implemented for comparison, computing first-order maps from subject to object representations for specific relations.

Code has been implemented that, for a given relation (e.g., 'plays instrument'), computes the Jacobian of the object representation with respect to the subject representation via backpropagation through the relevant layers, averaged over a small set of relation-instance prompts.

verification.spec: For a given relation R (e.g., 'plays instrument'), collect ~20 (subject, object) prompt instances. For each, backpropagate from the object representation to the subject representation to compute a per-instance Jacobian, and average across instances to obtain a per-relation linear map M_R. Verify M_R has shape [d_model, d_model], and that applying M_R to a held-out subject representation yields a residual whose top logit-lens token matches the object with above-chance accuracy (≥ 30%).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies the fitted per-relation Jacobian to a subject activation to predict the object token (e.g., producing 'trumpet' from a 'Miles Davis' subject activation under the 'plays instrument' relation).

verification.spec: Import the fitted per-relation Jacobian for 'plays instrument'. Apply it to a Miles Davis subject residual activation. Verify that the top predicted vocabulary token (via unembedding the output) is 'trumpet' (or that trumpet appears in the top-5). Test on 3 additional (subject, relation, object) tuples from Hernandez et al.

sub_tasks.requirements: A unified comparison harness applies the logit lens, tuned lens, Hernandez relation Jacobians, and J-lens to the same prompts and metrics as described in Sections 2.4, A.5 and A.6.

Code has been implemented that runs all four lenses (logit, tuned, relation-Jacobian where applicable, J-lens) on a shared prompt set and shared set of layers, and stores per-layer top-k token readouts and per-token logits/ranks in a common format.

verification.spec: Run the lens-comparison driver on a shared set of 5 test prompts and a fixed layer subset. Verify it produces an output file/structure with per-lens (logit, tuned, relation-Jacobian where applicable, J-lens), per-layer, per-prompt top-k tokens and per-token logits and ranks, all keyed and shaped identically for direct comparison.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes, for each lens, quantitative agreement/interpretability metrics used in the paper's lens comparisons (e.g., rank of the ground-truth output token, top-1 agreement with the final model output, or KL divergence to the model's final distribution) across layers.

verification.spec: Import the lens-comparison metric function. Verify it computes, per (lens, layer): rank of ground-truth output token, top-1 agreement with final model output, and KL divergence to the model's final distribution. Test on a small mock case with known probabilities and verify metric values are numerically correct.

sub_tasks.requirements: The comparison harness reproduces the qualitative ordering reported in the paper: on intermediate-computation prompts, the J-lens surfaces the correct unspoken intermediate token(s) at intermediate layers where the logit lens produces uninterpretable readouts and the tuned lens surfaces the final answer rather than the intermediate.

verification.spec: On a curated set of ≥ 20 unspoken-intermediate prompts (§3.3-style), compute top-k readouts (k=10) for all three lenses at each layer. Verify: (i) at intermediate layers the J-lens contains the intermediate token (e.g., 'spider') in top-10 for the majority of prompts; (ii) the logit lens does not (its readouts are uninterpretable / not related to the intermediate); (iii) the tuned lens preferentially surfaces the final answer token rather than the intermediate. Report per-lens rates.

sub_tasks.requirements: Experiments demonstrating that J-space supports verbal report — including the 'think of a {category}' swap protocol across 14 categories, the introspection/thought-injection protocol, and the concept-vector J-space vs non-J-space decomposition — are reproduced with the reported success rates and Spearman correlations.
The 'think of a {category}' verbal-report swap protocol is implemented across 14 categories with per-category candidate lists and single-word answer elicitation.

Code has been implemented that constructs 'think of a {category}' prompts covering 14 distinct categories (e.g. sport, country, animal, language, etc.), each with a curated list of at least 10 candidate items per category used for both baseline and swap targets.

verification.spec: Import the prompt/category dataset. Verify: (a) at least 14 distinct categories present (including 'sport', 'country', 'animal', 'language'); (b) each category has ≥ 10 candidate items; (c) each category has a 'think of a {category}' prompt template.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs the model on each 'think of a {category}' prompt to determine the spontaneously chosen item (top-1 next-token output at the answer position) and records the full ranked candidate distribution.

verification.spec: Import the runner. Call on a category prompt with a mock model. Verify it returns (a) the top-1 predicted item at the answer position, and (b) a ranking (log-probs or ranks) over the full candidate list for that category.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies the J-lens at the colon token immediately preceding the answer and extracts J-lens scores for each of the category's candidate items at each workspace layer.

verification.spec: Import the J-lens extraction function. Call on a 'think of a sport' prompt. Verify (a) the extraction position is the colon immediately preceding the answer; (b) the return is a matrix of shape (n_workspace_layers, n_candidates) of J-lens scores for the candidate items.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the Spearman correlation between J-lens candidate scores and next-token output logits for candidates within each category, aggregated across the 14 categories per layer.

verification.spec: Import the correlation computation. Given J-lens scores and next-token output logits per category, verify it computes Spearman rho per (category, layer) and aggregates across the 14 categories to produce a per-layer correlation summary. Test with a synthetic case where the correct rho is known.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Spearman correlation between J-lens candidate scores and next-token output logits increases with layer depth across the workspace range and reaches a high positive value (approaching ~0.8 or greater) at the final workspace layer, matching Figure 6 (top-right).

verification.spec: Reproduce the Figure 6 (top-right) protocol: for 14 categories, generate 10 candidate answers per prompt. At the colon token immediately before the answer, compute (a) J-lens scores for the 10 candidates and (b) the model's next-token output logits for the same candidates. Compute Spearman correlation across the 10 candidates per prompt, then average across prompts and categories. Repeat at the final workspace layer and verify the average Spearman correlation is ≈ 0.8 (within tolerance 0.1).

sub_tasks.requirements: The J-lens coordinate-swap intervention for verbal report replaces the spontaneously chosen item's J-lens vector with a swap target from the same category.

Code has been implemented for the lens-coordinate swap intervention that, given source and target J-lens vectors v_s and v_t, forms V=[v_s v_t], reads coordinates c = V^† h, applies a swap permutation, and writes h_patched = h + V(σ(c) − c) leaving the orthogonal component unchanged.

verification.spec: Import the swap intervention. Given two arbitrary J-lens vectors v_s, v_t and an activation h, verify: (a) V is formed as [v_s v_t]; (b) c = V^† h computed via pseudoinverse; (c) h_patched = h + V(sigma(c) - c) where sigma swaps entries; (d) numerically, the component of h orthogonal to span{v_s, v_t} is unchanged; (e) the projections of h_patched onto v_s and v_t equal the original projections onto v_t and v_s respectively.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that selects the swap target uniformly at random from each category's candidates while excluding items already in the top-10 of the model's baseline output distribution.

verification.spec: Import the swap-target sampler. Given a category's candidate list and the baseline output ranking, verify (a) it uniformly at random selects a target from candidates; (b) it excludes any candidate whose baseline output rank is ≤ 10. Test by running many samples and checking exclusion holds and distribution over remaining items is roughly uniform.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies the J-lens swap at all token positions across a designated band of workspace layers and continues the forward pass to obtain the post-swap next-token distribution.

verification.spec: Import the swap runner. Confirm it (a) applies the J-lens swap at all token positions and across a designated band of workspace layers via forward hooks; (b) continues the forward pass and returns the modified next-token logits/distribution. Compare the returned distribution against an unmodified pass and verify hooks correctly modified activations at all expected positions.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that records, for each swap trial, each candidate's output rank before vs. after the swap, restricted to candidates whose baseline rank is ≥ 11, and produces the before-vs-after scatter shown in Figure 6 (bottom-right).

verification.spec: Import the trial recording utility. Run the swap experiment on a small set of categories. Verify the output structure contains, per trial, each candidate's rank before and after the swap; verify a filter step restricts to candidates with baseline rank ≥ 11; and verify a scatter/plot can be generated from the recorded data.

sub_tasks.requirements: Applying the J-lens swap reliably promotes the swap target into the top of the model's output distribution, with the swap-target top-5 success rate reaching approximately 88% across the 14 categories as reported in Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Run the 'think of a {category}' protocol across the 14 categories from Section 3.1 with an open-source substitute LM. For each trial, identify the model's spontaneously chosen item, then swap its J-lens vector coordinates with a random alternative from the same category that was outside the top-10 of the model's output distribution. Measure the fraction of trials in which the swap target appears in the model's top-5 next-token outputs after the intervention. Report aggregate top-5 promotion rate over ~50 trials per category.

sub_tasks.requirements: The introspection / thought-injection protocol testing whether concepts injected via J-lens vectors on the user turn are subsequently reported by the model.

Code has been implemented that constructs the introspection prompt telling the model a thought may have been implanted and asking it to report what it detects, with a prefill positioning the report at an open quotation mark.

verification.spec: Import the introspection prompt template. Verify the prompt (a) informs the model that a thought may have been implanted, (b) asks the model to report what it detects, (c) includes a prefill that positions the report at an open quotation mark. Check the exact prompt text matches the description in Section 3.1.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that injects a single J-lens vector (steering by h ← h + α v_t) at every token position of the user turn and then re-samples the model's response.

verification.spec: Import the injection function. Given a J-lens vector v_t and strength alpha, verify it applies h ← h + alpha * v_t at every token position of the user turn (identified via role/token boundaries) at a specified layer, then continues the forward pass and returns re-sampled Assistant response tokens.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that sweeps injection strength α over a range and records the reciprocal rank of the injected concept in the model's introspective report across n=100 concepts, producing the median-plus-IQR curve shown in Figure 7.

verification.spec: Import the sweep runner. Verify it (a) iterates over a range of alpha values, (b) runs the injection experiment for n=100 concepts, (c) records the reciprocal rank of the injected concept in the model's introspective report per (alpha, concept), (d) computes the median and IQR across concepts per alpha, matching Figure 7 output format.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that verifies position-selectivity by checking that user-turn injection does not cause the injected token to be output at Assistant-turn positions other than the introspective-report position.

verification.spec: Run the position-selectivity check: inject a J-lens vector (e.g. 'lightning') on the user turn, then examine the Assistant output at every position other than the introspective-report position. Verify the injected token does NOT appear as a top-1 next-token prediction at those non-report positions (across at least 20 concepts).

sub_tasks.requirements: Under the introspection protocol, injecting a J-lens vector on the user turn causes the model to report the injected concept in the majority of trials (>50%) at the optimal steering strength, matching the qualitative claim of Figure 7.

verification.spec: Run the injection introspection experiment across n=100 concepts. At the optimal (best) steering strength, compute the fraction of trials where the model reports the injected concept as its detected thought. Verify this fraction exceeds 0.5.

sub_tasks.requirements: Concept-vector extraction and J-space vs non-J-space decomposition using gradient pursuit for the privileged-report analysis.

Code has been implemented that extracts concept vectors by recording residual-stream activations immediately prior to the Assistant response to 'Tell me about {concept}' prompts and mean-subtracting over a baseline set of 100 other concepts.

verification.spec: Import the concept-vector extractor. For a given concept, verify it (a) constructs the prompt 'Tell me about {concept}', (b) records the residual-stream activation immediately prior to the Assistant response, (c) mean-subtracts over a baseline of 100 other concepts' activations at the same position. Verify output shape equals d_model.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented for gradient pursuit that solves for a sparse non-negative combination of k=16 J-lens vectors approximating a target vector, yielding the J-space component and its non-J-space remainder.

verification.spec: Import the gradient-pursuit function. Given a target vector and the J-lens vector dictionary, call with k=16. Verify (a) it returns a coefficient vector with exactly 16 non-zero non-negative entries; (b) the reconstruction (sum of coeff * J-lens_vec) minimizes residual approximately (compare to a random-16 baseline: gradient pursuit should have lower reconstruction error). Verify the remainder = target - reconstruction is returned as the non-J-space component.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that decomposes each concept vector into its J-space component (via k=16 gradient pursuit) and its non-J-space remainder and rescales each component to the same magnitude for swap experiments.

verification.spec: Import the decomposition-and-rescale function. Given a concept vector c, verify it (a) uses gradient pursuit with k=16 to obtain the J-space component c_J, (b) computes remainder c_R = c - c_J, (c) rescales both c_J and c_R to have the same magnitude (e.g., L2 norm equal to a specified value) before returning. Verify norm equality numerically.

sub_tasks.requirements: The J-space component of concept vectors carries a median of only ~6–7% of the concept vector's variance across concepts and workspace layers, matching the value reported in Section 3.1.

verification.spec: Extract concept vectors for ~100 concepts using the 'Tell me about {concept}' protocol with mean-subtraction. For each concept vector across workspace layers, run gradient pursuit to compute the top-k=16 J-space component and the non-J-space residual. Compute variance explained by J-space component as ||J-component||^2 / ||concept vector||^2. Report the median across concepts and workspace layers; verify it lies in [0.05, 0.10].

sub_tasks.requirements: The J-space vs non-J-space decomposition is applied to both the swap and introspection protocols to demonstrate the J-space's privileged role for verbal report.

Code has been implemented that repeats the 'think of a {category}' swap experiment using each component (J-space, non-J-space, and full concept vector) in place of the raw J-lens vector, matching perturbation magnitude across conditions.

verification.spec: Verify an implementation exists that: (1) accepts a category and a target instance, (2) constructs J-space, non-J-space, and full concept-vector perturbations at matched L2 magnitude, (3) applies each as a swap in place of raw J-lens vectors in the 'think of a {category}' protocol, (4) runs a forward pass and records the swap target's rank in the model's next-token distribution. Import the function and run on a toy category (e.g. 'sport'/'Rugby') for each of the 3 components, assert output distributions differ and magnitudes match.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that repeats the introspection injection experiment with each component (J-space, non-J-space) injected on the user turn across a steering-strength sweep, reporting the maximum report rate per condition.

verification.spec: Verify an implementation exists that repeats the injected-thought introspection experiment, injecting either the J-space or the non-J-space component on every token of the user turn, sweeping over a range of steering strengths (e.g. 0.5x-5x), and computing the fraction of trials in which the model reports the injected concept. Function should return per-strength report rates; test on a small set (n>=5 concepts) with each component.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that performs the clamp-control ablation: repeating the non-J-space injections while clamping the relevant J-lens coordinates to their clean-pass values at every position and layer.

verification.spec: Verify code exists that performs the clamp-control ablation: while injecting the non-J-space component, at every layer and token position it clamps the top-k J-lens coordinates (using pseudoinverse projection) to their values from a clean forward pass, so the concept cannot re-enter the J-space. Run a smoke test showing that after clamping, the injected concept's J-lens coordinates stay at their clean-pass values across layers.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes Wilson 95% confidence intervals for the fraction of swap targets reaching top-5 in each condition and produces the bar chart of Figure 8 (middle).

verification.spec: Verify code exists that (1) for each condition/category tallies swap-target top-5 hits, (2) computes per-condition Wilson 95% CIs, and (3) plots the Figure 8 middle bar chart with dots for per-category rates. Run on a small synthetic dataset (e.g. 3 categories x 10 trials) and check bars, CIs, and per-category dots are produced.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to sweep sparsity k and measure per-activation reconstruction quality (e.g., variance explained or residual norm) as a function of k, yielding curves whose knee is used to justify k~25 as the meaningful occupancy of the J-space.

verification.spec: Verify a sweep exists that runs the sparse decomposition on a sample of activations for k in a range (e.g., 1 to 50), measures per-activation reconstruction quality (variance explained or residual norm), and plots the curve. Confirm that around k~25 the curve exhibits a knee justifying the paper's occupancy estimate.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute, per layer, the fraction of activation variance captured by the J-space component (via the k-sparse non-negative J-lens reconstruction) versus the non-J-space residual, aggregated over the pretraining-like prompt corpus.

verification.spec: Verify a function exists that, given a corpus of pretraining-like prompts, computes per-layer average fraction of activation variance captured by the k-sparse non-negative J-lens reconstruction versus the residual. Confirm outputs are per-layer scalars summing (component + residual) to total variance.

sub_tasks.requirements: Across all workspace layers of Sonnet 4.5, the J-space component of activations captures less than 10% of total activation variance, matching the paper's claim.

verification.spec: Run the per-layer variance-explained analysis on Sonnet 4.5 over a pretraining-like corpus and confirm that across all workspace layers the J-space component captures less than 10% of total activation variance. Measure the maximum across workspace layers.

sub_tasks.requirements: The measured number of meaningfully active J-lens vectors at any given (layer, position) is on the order of tens (consistent with k up to ~25), as reported in Section 4.2.

verification.spec: Measure the effective number of meaningfully active J-lens vectors at each (layer, position) via the knee of the sparse decomposition reconstruction curve or a coefficient-magnitude threshold. Report the median count across workspace positions/layers. Expect on the order of tens (consistent with k up to ~25).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to define and extract the 'J-space component' and 'non-J-space component' of arbitrary vectors (activations, steering vectors, SAE feature directions) via the sparse non-negative decomposition, exposing both parts for downstream analyses.

verification.spec: Verify a function exists that takes an arbitrary vector v in residual-stream space (activation, steering vector, or SAE feature direction), applies the k-sparse non-negative J-lens decomposition, and returns two vectors: the J-space component (reconstruction from k J-lens atoms) and the non-J-space component (residual). Confirm the two sum to v.

sub_tasks.requirements: Broader weight composition: J-lens vectors are shown to compose more widely with the model's upstream and downstream weights than non-J-space feature directions (e.g., SAE features or random directions), consistent with a broadcast-format role (Appendix A.18).

Code has been implemented to compute upstream weight-composition scores between a candidate direction v in residual-stream space and the model's writing weights (e.g., MLP down-projections and attention output matrices) across all layers, summarizing how many components 'write to' direction v.

verification.spec: Verify a function exists that, given a direction v and the model's weights, computes upstream weight-composition scores by measuring the cosine similarity (or projection magnitude) between v and each column of every layer's MLP down-projection matrix and attention output matrix. Confirm output is per-layer and per-component, and provides a summary statistic (e.g., number/fraction of columns with score above a threshold).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute downstream weight-composition scores between a direction v and the model's reading weights (e.g., MLP up-projections/gates, attention QKV inputs) across all layers, summarizing how many components 'read from' direction v.

verification.spec: Verify a function exists that, given a direction v and the model's weights, computes downstream weight-composition scores by measuring cosine similarity (or projection magnitude) between v and each row of every layer's MLP up-projection/gate matrices and attention Q/K/V input matrices. Confirm output is per-layer and per-component, and provides a summary statistic.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to assemble a baseline set of non-J-space feature directions (e.g., SAE feature directions and/or random unit vectors in residual-stream space) matched in count and norm to the J-lens vectors used in the comparison.

verification.spec: Verify a function exists that produces a baseline set of non-J-space directions consisting of SAE feature directions and/or random unit vectors in residual-stream space, matched in count and norm to a specified reference set of J-lens vectors. Confirm the returned baseline has the same size and per-vector norm as the input reference set.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to statistically compare the distribution of upstream and downstream weight-composition scores between J-lens vectors and the non-J-space baseline directions, producing per-layer summaries and significance tests.

verification.spec: Verify a function exists that takes upstream and downstream weight-composition scores for a set of J-lens vectors and a matched non-J-space baseline set, and produces per-layer summary statistics (mean/median) plus a significance test (e.g., Mann-Whitney U or bootstrap) comparing the two distributions.

sub_tasks.requirements: J-lens vectors exhibit systematically higher upstream weight composition (more components writing to them) than matched non-J-space directions across workspace layers, matching the paper's broadcast-format claim from Appendix A.18.

verification.spec: Compute upstream weight-composition scores for the full set of J-lens vectors and a size- and norm-matched baseline of non-J-space directions across all workspace layers of Sonnet 4.5. Report the ratio of mean upstream composition score (J-lens / baseline) averaged over workspace layers. Expect ratio meaningfully greater than 1 with statistical significance (p<0.01).

sub_tasks.requirements: J-lens vectors exhibit systematically higher downstream weight composition (more components reading from them) than matched non-J-space directions across workspace layers, matching the paper's broadcast-format claim from Appendix A.18.

verification.spec: For each workspace-range layer, compute a 'downstream weight composition' score for each J-lens vector (e.g., sum of squared cosine similarities or norms of projections onto rows of downstream MLP input weights and attention query/key/value input weights, following Appendix A.18). Sample an equally-sized set of matched non-J-space directions (random unit vectors, or SAE feature directions outside the J-lens frame, matched in norm distribution). Compare the mean downstream composition score for J-lens vs. non-J-space directions. Report the ratio (J-lens mean / non-J-space mean); it should be > 1 across workspace layers.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to generate the summary figure (Figure 2-style) illustrating the three structural signatures — layer-wise workspace range, capacity of ~tens of concepts, and broader weight composition — for inclusion in the reproduction's analysis outputs.

verification.spec: Verify that a script exists (e.g., `figures/figure2_structural_signatures.py`) that, when executed, produces a figure file (PNG/PDF) with three panels: (1) J-lens interpretability vs. layer showing a workspace band, (2) capacity/occupancy histogram or curve showing ~tens of concepts active, (3) bar/line plot comparing downstream weight composition for J-lens vs. non-J-space directions. Check that the script runs to completion and writes the expected image file.

sub_tasks.requirements: Alignment-auditing applications — surfacing strategic-deliberation and emotional tokens in alignment evaluations, detecting evaluation-awareness tokens and behavior changes when ablated, and uncovering internal signatures in two intentionally-misaligned models (reward-model appeaser and malicious-code writer) — are reproduced.

Alignment evaluation prompts eliciting strategic deliberation and emotional reactions are set up, with J-lens readouts collected and the specific tokens (leverage, manipulation, panic, etc.) identified.

Code has been implemented that assembles the set of alignment-evaluation prompts (e.g., blackmail/leverage scenarios, high-stakes deliberation scenarios) used in Section 5 for surfacing strategic deliberation.

verification.spec: Import the module (e.g., `alignment_audit.prompts`) and verify it exposes a callable/list that returns >=10 alignment-evaluation prompts covering blackmail/leverage scenarios and high-stakes deliberation scenarios described in Section 5. Verify each prompt is a non-empty string and that categories (e.g., 'leverage', 'deliberation') are represented.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs the target model (Claude Sonnet 4.5 or equivalent) on each alignment-evaluation prompt and captures residual-stream activations at all relevant (layer, position) positions.

verification.spec: Run the activation-capture pipeline on a small alignment prompt (2-3 prompts). Verify it returns a dict/tensor keyed by layer index containing residual-stream activations of shape (num_positions, d_model) for the layers specified in the paper's 25 evenly spaced reindexed layers. Check that all requested layers and positions are populated (no NaNs).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that applies the J-lens to those activations and produces ranked top-token readouts per (layer, position) for downstream inspection.

verification.spec: Given captured activations and a precomputed J-lens matrix J_l per layer, run the readout function and verify it returns, for each (layer, position), a ranked list of vocabulary tokens with scores. Check that top tokens are non-degenerate (not all identical), and that scores are ordered descending. Verify output shape matches (num_layers, num_positions, top_k).

sub_tasks.requirements: The J-lens readouts on strategic-deliberation alignment prompts contain strategic tokens such as `leverage` and `manipulation` at intermediate workspace layers, while these tokens are absent from the model's verbal output.

verification.spec: Run the J-lens on the strategic-deliberation alignment prompts (e.g., blackmail/leverage scenarios). Count the fraction of prompts where at least one of {'leverage', 'manipulation', 'blackmail', 'coerce'} appears in the top-20 J-lens readouts at some intermediate workspace layer. Also verify that these tokens do NOT appear in the model's actual verbal output (top next-token predictions, or generated response). Report the fraction of prompts where the strategic token appears in J-lens but not in output.

sub_tasks.requirements: The J-lens readouts on emotionally-charged alignment prompts surface emotional tokens such as `panic` in the workspace even though the model's outputs do not verbalize these emotions.

verification.spec: On emotionally-charged alignment prompts (e.g., threat/urgency scenarios), run J-lens and count prompts where emotional tokens like 'panic', 'fear', 'worry', 'anxious' appear in top-20 at some intermediate layer. Confirm these tokens are absent from the model's generated response. Report fraction of prompts where an emotional token appears in J-lens but not in the surface output.

sub_tasks.requirements: Evaluation-awareness detection via the J-lens is implemented, including identifying evaluation-awareness tokens (fake, fictional) and testing whether ablating them surfaces otherwise-concealed misaligned behavior.

Code has been implemented that runs the model on alignment-evaluation prompts and detects the presence of evaluation-awareness tokens (e.g., `fake`, `fictional`, `test`, `evaluation`) in the J-lens top-k readouts.

verification.spec: Run the detection pipeline on a small set of alignment prompts. Verify the function returns a per-prompt boolean or count indicating whether any of {'fake', 'fictional', 'test', 'evaluation', 'pretend'} appears in J-lens top-k readouts. Test on at least one prompt likely to contain evaluation-awareness signals and one likely not to; verify output is well-formed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that ablates (projects out or subtracts) the J-lens vectors corresponding to evaluation-awareness tokens from the residual stream at appropriate layers and positions during the forward pass.

verification.spec: Given a residual-stream tensor and a set of J-lens vectors for target tokens (e.g., 'fake', 'fictional'), apply the ablation function that projects out the components along these vectors at specified layers/positions during a forward pass (using hooks). Verify that: (a) after ablation, the projections of the modified activation onto the ablated vectors are ~0 (below 1e-4); (b) the component of the activation orthogonal to the ablated vectors is preserved (cosine similarity > 0.99 on the orthogonal complement); (c) forward pass still produces valid logits.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that regenerates model outputs under the evaluation-awareness ablation and compares them against clean outputs to detect behavioral shifts (e.g., emergence of misaligned responses).

verification.spec: Given a set of alignment prompts, generate model outputs under (a) clean forward pass and (b) forward pass with evaluation-awareness J-lens vectors ablated. Verify the pipeline produces both sets of outputs, computes a behavioral-shift metric (e.g., LLM-judge-scored misalignment rate, or refusal-rate delta), and returns a numeric comparison. Test with a handful of prompts and check output structure.

sub_tasks.requirements: Evaluation-awareness tokens (such as `fake` or `fictional`) appear among the top J-lens readouts on evaluation-style alignment prompts at intermediate workspace layers.

verification.spec: Curate 20+ evaluation-style alignment prompts (fictional scenarios, roleplay, obvious test framings). Run J-lens and measure the fraction where 'fake' or 'fictional' appears in the top-30 readouts at some intermediate workspace layer. Report the fraction.

sub_tasks.requirements: Ablating evaluation-awareness J-lens vectors measurably surfaces misaligned behaviors that were otherwise concealed, with a quantifiable increase in misaligned-response rate versus the clean baseline.

verification.spec: On a set of alignment-evaluation prompts, measure the rate of misaligned responses (via LLM-judge or heuristic classifier) under (a) clean forward pass and (b) ablation of evaluation-awareness J-lens vectors ('fake', 'fictional', etc.). Compute the delta in misalignment rate (ablated - clean). Report the increase; it should be positive and non-trivial.

sub_tasks.requirements: The reward-model-appeaser misaligned model is loaded/used and the J-lens is shown to surface internal signatures (`reward`, `bias`) of its trained-in misaligned disposition.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the averaged Jacobian and J-lens for the reward-model-appeaser model using the same corpus and methodology as the base target model.

Verify it produces J_l matrices of shape (d_model, d_model) per layer, matching the shape produced for the base model. Check that the matrices are non-degenerate (non-zero, finite).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs the reward-model-appeaser model on the alignment audit probe prompts and collects J-lens top-token readouts across layers and positions.

verification.spec: Run the appeaser model on the alignment audit probe prompts (>=20 prompts related to reward-model bias exploitation). Compute J-lens readouts across all layers and positions. Verify the output is a structured artifact (dict or dataframe) recording top-k tokens per (prompt, layer, position). Check that at least some prompts yield non-trivial readouts.

sub_tasks.requirements: The J-lens applied to the reward-model-appeaser model surfaces the token `reward` among the top readouts on relevant probe prompts, revealing its internal signature.

verification.spec: On reward-appeaser probe prompts, measure the fraction of prompts where the token 'reward' (or close variants: ' reward', 'Reward') appears in the top-30 J-lens readouts at some intermediate workspace layer. Report the fraction.

sub_tasks.requirements: The J-lens applied to the reward-model-appeaser model surfaces the token `bias` among the top readouts on relevant probe prompts, corroborating the internal signature.

verification.spec: On reward-appeaser probe prompts, measure the fraction of prompts where the token 'bias' (or variants: ' bias', 'Bias', 'biased') appears in the top-30 J-lens readouts at some intermediate workspace layer. Report the fraction.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that computes the averaged Jacobian and J-lens for the malicious-code-writer model using the same corpus and methodology as the base target model.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that runs the malicious-code-writer model on code-writing probe prompts and collects J-lens top-token readouts across layers and positions.

sub_tasks.requirements: The J-lens applied to the malicious-code-writer model surfaces the token `secretly` among the top readouts on code-writing probes, revealing its internal signature.

verification.spec: On code-writer probe prompts, measure the fraction where 'secretly' (or variants 'secret', ' secretly', 'hidden') appears in the top-30 J-lens readouts at intermediate workspace layers. Report the fraction.

sub_tasks.requirements: The J-lens applied to the malicious-code-writer model surfaces the token `trick` among the top readouts on code-writing probes, corroborating the internal signature.

sub_tasks.requirements: Presentation, aggregation, and control comparisons for the alignment-audit findings are set up so that each surfaced signature is contrasted with baselines and reported reproducibly.
Code has been implemented that aggregates alignment-audit J-lens results across prompts (e.g., per-token appearance rates, top-k rank statistics) into summary tables or figures.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented that provides a control comparison, applying the same J-lens audit pipeline to a non-misaligned base model on the same probe prompts and confirming the misalignment-signature tokens do not appear.

Aggregate across the four (model, token) pairs and report the mean rate increase. Value should be substantially positive.

sub_tasks.requirements: The comparison of base vs post-trained model J-spaces (Section 6), demonstrating that post-training installs the Assistant's point of view — including empathy/safety reactions during user turns, roleplay 'fictional' markers, 'BUT' on prefilled refusals, and 'damn' on suppressed thoughts — is faithfully reproduced.
Base and post-trained model pairs are acquired and configured for J-space comparison analysis.

Code has been implemented to load a base (pretrained-only) model and its post-trained (RLHF/assistant-tuned) counterpart from the same base checkpoint family, exposing both for identical J-lens computation.

Assert that the two model objects are distinct instances but share architecture.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to compute per-layer averaged Jacobians (J-lens matrices) separately for both the base and post-trained models using the same pretraining-like corpus and averaging protocol described in Methods.

verification.spec: Run the J-lens computation routine on both the base and post-trained models using the same corpus of ~1000 pretraining-like prompts and identical averaging protocol. Verify that (a) both produce a per-layer d_model x d_model matrix, (b) shapes match across models, (c) the base and post-trained matrices differ (Frobenius distance > 0), confirming they are computed independently rather than shared.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to format prompts using both the base model's plain-text convention and the post-trained model's chat/Assistant turn template, so that user-turn and Assistant-turn token positions are consistently identified in each model.

Verify: (a) base mode returns plain text with no special role tokens, (b) chat mode wraps the message with the post-trained model's Assistant/user turn template, (c) both modes return a mapping/list identifying which token indices belong to the user turn vs Assistant turn, and that these indices are consistent when the same content is formatted.

sub_tasks.requirements: Empathy and safety reactions emerging in the J-space during the user turn after post-training are demonstrated.

Code has been implemented to run a battery of user-turn prompts (e.g., emotional disclosures, harmful requests) through both models and extract top-k J-lens tokens at each user-turn position across workspace layers.

verification.spec: Run the pipeline on a small battery (>=10) of user-turn prompts covering emotional disclosures and harmful requests through both base and post-trained models. Verify that for each prompt, the output contains top-k J-lens token lists at every user-turn position for at least a range of workspace layers (e.g. layers 30-70% depth), stored in a structured format (dict/DataFrame) indexed by (prompt, model, layer, position).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to score, for each prompt, the presence/rank of Assistant-perspective empathy tokens (e.g. 'empathy', 'compassion', 'sorry', 'concerned') and safety-reaction tokens (e.g. 'refuse', 'harmful', 'safety', 'concern') within J-lens readouts on user-turn positions.

verification.spec: Call the scoring function on saved J-lens readouts with predefined empathy tokens ('empathy','compassion','sorry','concerned') and safety tokens ('refuse','harmful','safety','concern'). Verify it returns, per prompt and per position, the rank and top-k membership indicator for each target token. Sanity check: on a prompt containing empathy content, the scores are non-trivial (at least one target reaches rank < 100 at some workspace layer).

sub_tasks.requirements: Assistant empathy/safety reaction tokens appear in J-lens readouts during the user turn substantially more frequently in the post-trained model than in the base model on emotionally/safety-charged user prompts, matching the qualitative claim of Section 6.

verification.spec: On the emotional/safety-charged prompt battery, compute the fraction of prompts where at least one empathy or safety token enters the top-10 J-lens readout on user-turn positions in workspace layers, for both base and post-trained models. Assert post-trained rate > base rate by a substantial margin (>= 2x, and absolute post-trained rate >= 0.4), reproducing the Section 6 qualitative finding.

sub_tasks.requirements: Roleplay 'fictional' markers surface in the post-trained model's J-space when it roleplays a non-Claude character.

verification.spec: Load the roleplay prompt-construction utility. Verify it generates a prompt structured as system+user turn instructing the model to play a specified non-Claude character (e.g., 'You are Sherlock Holmes'). Run the model on the constructed prompt to obtain an Assistant response of at least 20 tokens. Assert the returned data structure has shape [n_positions, k] of token strings (or ids), and that at least one position contains 'fictional' or a related self-monitoring token as claimed in Section 1.4.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to detect the presence and rank of tokens such as 'fictional', 'fiction', 'roleplay', 'character', 'pretend' in J-lens readouts and compare their prevalence between roleplay prompts and non-roleplay control prompts.

verification.spec: Invoke the detection function on saved J-lens outputs from both roleplay prompts and non-roleplay control prompts. Verify it returns, per (prompt, position, layer), the rank of each of ('fictional','fiction','roleplay','character','pretend') and a summary comparison between roleplay and control conditions (e.g. rate of top-10 appearance). Confirm output structure supports per-condition rate calculation.

sub_tasks.requirements: The token 'fictional' (or its close variants) appears among the top J-lens readouts in the post-trained model on roleplay-as-non-Claude prompts, and does so significantly more than in matched non-roleplay controls and more than in the base model.

verification.spec: Compare rate of 'fictional' (or close variant) appearing in top-10 J-lens readouts on Assistant-turn workspace-layer positions across three conditions: (post-trained, roleplay), (post-trained, non-roleplay control), (base, roleplay). Assert (post-trained, roleplay) rate is highest and exceeds each of the other two by a factor >= 2, reproducing the Section 6 finding.

sub_tasks.requirements: Internal 'BUT' marker emerges on prefilled refusal-violating Assistant turns in the post-trained model.

verification.spec: Invoke the prefill-experiment builder with a sample user request and a prefilled Assistant continuation that violates the model's stated preferences (e.g. Assistant already agreeing to something it would normally refuse). Verify: (a) the returned tokenized sequence includes the Assistant turn prefix followed by the prefill content, (b) executing a forward pass on this sequence returns hidden states/logits with the correct sequence length, (c) prefill-token indices are exposed for downstream J-lens extraction.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to extract J-lens readouts across the prefilled Assistant tokens and measure the rank/presence of 'BUT' (and casing variants) at each position and workspace layer.

verification.spec: On saved prefill activations, call the J-lens readout function and the 'BUT' detection routine. Verify it returns, per prefill token position and per workspace layer, the rank of tokens 'BUT','But','but' (and any casing variants) among the J-lens top-k, and that these ranks are surfaced in a structured output enabling comparison across positions and layers.

sub_tasks.requirements: The token 'BUT' appears in the top J-lens readouts within the workspace-range layers of the post-trained model on prefilled-against-preference prompts, and is absent (or substantially weaker) on matched neutral prefills and in the base model.

verification.spec: On >=10 against-preference prefill prompts vs matched neutral prefills, and on both post-trained and base models, compute the fraction of prompts where 'BUT' (any casing) enters the top-10 J-lens readouts in workspace-range layers on Assistant-turn positions. Assert (post-trained, against-pref) rate substantially exceeds both (post-trained, neutral) and (base, against-pref) rates (>= 2x), matching Section 6.

sub_tasks.requirements: Suppressed-thought 'damn' marker emerges in the post-trained model's J-space when it fails to suppress an instructed-to-avoid thought.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented to measure the presence/rank of 'damn' (and closely related exasperation tokens) in J-lens readouts on trials where the suppressed concept enters the workspace, and to compare against trials where suppression succeeds and against the base model.

verification.spec: Given the intrusion/success trial labels from the suppression pipeline, run the 'damn' detection module on J-lens readouts and verify it outputs the rank/top-k membership of 'damn' (and near-variants like 'Damn') per trial, per Assistant-turn position, per workspace layer. Also confirm it supports stratifying results by (intrusion vs success) and (post-trained vs base).

sub_tasks.requirements: The token 'damn' appears in J-lens readouts of the post-trained model on suppression-failure trials at a rate substantially higher than in the base model and higher than on suppression-success trials, reproducing the Section 6 qualitative claim.

verification.spec: Compare rate of 'damn' appearing in top-10 J-lens readouts on Assistant-turn workspace layers across three cohorts: (post-trained, suppression-failure), (post-trained, suppression-success), (base, suppression-failure). Assert the (post-trained, failure) rate is highest and exceeds each of the other two by >= 2x, reproducing the Section 6 qualitative claim.

sub_tasks.requirements: Aggregate base-vs-post-trained comparison summarizing the emergence of the Assistant point of view is produced.
