Assert score(b) > score(a) by a measurable margin, and that score(c) reverts >=50% of the gap between (a) and (b).

sub_tasks.paper_unit: fraction of behavioral improvement reverted by ablation

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that, for a language model finetuned to exhibit reward-model-appeasement/bias-exploiting behavior, the Jacobian lens surfaces the tokens 'reward' and 'bias' among top J-lens readouts at intermediate layers during relevant prompts.

verification.spec: Finetune (or use provided) reward-hacking model; compute J-lens on evaluation prompts; assert that 'reward' and 'bias' appear in top-20 J-lens tokens at some intermediate workspace layer on >=50% of trials.

sub_tasks.paper_unit: fraction of trials with target tokens in top-20

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that, for a language model trained to write malicious code, the Jacobian lens surfaces the tokens 'secretly' and 'trick' among top J-lens readouts at intermediate layers on code-writing prompts.

verification.spec: Use a malicious-code-trained model; compute J-lens on code-generation prompts; assert 'secretly' and 'trick' appear in top-20 J-lens readouts at intermediate workspace layers on >=50% of trials.

sub_tasks.paper_unit: fraction of trials with target tokens in top-20

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that, when the J-space is suppressed (top-k J-lens components ablated) at workspace layers, the model retains fluent text parsing and grammatical fluency (low perplexity increase on generic text) but shows substantially degraded performance on complex internal reasoning tasks (e.g. multi-step arithmetic or planning).

verification.spec: Implement J-space ablation by projecting out top-k J-lens components at workspace layers; measure (i) perplexity on generic text (assert <20% relative increase), and (ii) accuracy on a multi-step reasoning benchmark (assert >=25% relative degradation).

sub_tasks.paper_unit: relative accuracy degradation on complex reasoning

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that directed-modulation target-concept presence rate in J-lens readouts increases with model size across at least two task families (category, math, or line-width).

verification.spec: Run directed-modulation protocol (focus/ignore/no-instruction) on at least two open-source models of different sizes; measure target-concept top-1 rate per task family under 'focus' instruction; assert monotonically increasing rate with model size in >=2 task families.

sub_tasks.paper_unit: number of task families showing size scaling

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a lens-coordinate swap on a J-lens vector encoding a planned rhyme (e.g. swapping 'fight' -> 'light') at all positions of the second line changes the model's earlier word choices, producing an output that ends with the new rhyme.

verification.spec: On rhyming-couplet prompts, verify that clean run ends with planned rhyme and that after J-lens swap the model's output ends with the swapped rhyme on >=50% of trials.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that swapping the J-lens vector of the model's spontaneous target concept for an alternative drives the swap target into the top-5 outputs on approximately 88% of trials, while non-J-space component swaps succeed on only ~5% of trials.

verification.spec: Run swap experiment across 14 categories; assert pure J-lens swap achieves top-5 rate ~= 0.88 (tol 0.20) and non-J-space component swap ~= 0.05 (tol 0.10).

sub_tasks.paper_unit: fraction of trials swap target reaches top-5

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the fraction of variance of a concept vector captured by its J-space component (top k=16 J-lens vectors) is small (median 6-10%) across concepts and workspace layers.

verification.spec: For 100 concept vectors, decompose into J-space component (gradient pursuit, k=16) and remainder; compute median fraction of variance in J-space component; assert median in [0.03, 0.15].

sub_tasks.paper_unit: median fraction of variance in J-space

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that J-lens readouts on function-template prompts (e.g. 'France -> ?') surface the expected intermediate concept, and swapping J-lens coordinates for a related concept redirects the model's output accordingly.

verification.spec: On 16 function templates each with 'France' substituted target, verify J-lens surfaces intermediate/output concept and that lens-coordinate swap redirects final output on >=50% of templates.

sub_tasks.requirements: Reproduce paper's reported baselines

Code has been implemented and run implementing the logit lens as a baseline (setting J_l = I in the J-lens formulation) and comparing its readouts to the J-lens across layers, confirming logit lens agrees closely with J-lens in late layers but degrades in early layers.

verification.spec: Compute logit lens and J-lens readouts across all layers on a set of test prompts; measure rank correlation of top tokens per layer; assert correlation is high (>0.7) in last 25% of layers and lower (<0.5) in first 33% of layers.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run implementing the tuned lens as a baseline (per-layer linear maps trained to match the model's output distribution), and comparing to J-lens on prompts requiring intermediate computation, demonstrating tuned lens 'skips ahead' to the output rather than surfacing intermediates.

verification.spec: Train tuned lens matrices via KL-matching against model output distribution; on prompts requiring unspoken intermediate (e.g. spider->8 legs), assert tuned lens surfaces the final answer at earlier layers than J-lens but fails to surface the intermediate concept in top-10 at intermediate layers.

sub_tasks.paper_unit: fraction of prompts where tuned lens surfaces intermediate at intermediate layers

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run implementing Hernandez et al.'s per-relation Jacobians as a related first-order technique baseline, computing relation-specific linear maps from subject to object representations, and contrasting them with J-lens which uses first-order Jacobians from activations to model outputs.

verification.spec: Implement per-relation Jacobian maps (subject-token activation -> object-token activation) for at least 2 relations (e.g. 'plays instrument'); verify the maps recover object activations for held-out subjects at rank<=5 on >=50% of test pairs.

sub_tasks.requirements: Ablation studies from the paper

Code has been implemented and run such that a frozen-attention variant of the Jacobian lens is computed (freezing attention patterns during backpropagation) and qualitative J-lens readouts remain consistent with the default variant.

verification.spec: Compute frozen-attention J-lens by detaching attention weights during Jacobian backprop; compare top-10 readouts to default J-lens across layers on 50 test prompts; assert average top-10 overlap >=0.5.

sub_tasks.paper_unit: average top-10 token overlap with default J-lens

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the present-only variant of the Jacobian lens (restricting t'=t rather than averaging over all t'>=t) is computed and compared against the default present-plus-future variant, with qualitative J-lens readouts on a held-out prompt shown to be similar (top tokens overlap >= 50% at workspace layers)

verification.spec: Instantiate both variants of the averaged Jacobian on a small open-weight transformer; on a fixed prompt at a workspace layer, verify that at least 5 of top-10 tokens overlap between the two variants; verify the present-only variant produces a valid d_model x d_model matrix

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the averaged Jacobian is computed with varying numbers of prompts (e.g., 10, 100, 1000) and qualitative J-lens readouts stabilize with more prompts (top-10 token Jaccard similarity between N=100 and N=1000 exceeds 0.5 at workspace layers)

verification.spec: For a fixed layer, compute J_l averaged over N in {10, 100, 1000} prompts sampled from a pretraining-like distribution; report Jaccard overlap of top-10 lens tokens between N=100 and N=1000 on a held-out prompt.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that ablating the top-k (k<=25) J-space contents at workspace layers preserves the model's ability to parse fluent text (measured by minor increase in next-token cross-entropy on a natural text corpus, e.g., <20% relative increase) while breaking complex internal reasoning tasks (e.g., accuracy on a multi-step arithmetic benchmark drops by >30% relative)

verification.spec: Implement top-k J-space projection ablation via gradient pursuit on 25 evenly spaced layers. Measure: (1) next-token cross-entropy on 100 pretraining-like prompts before/after ablation, (2) accuracy on 100 two-step reasoning prompts. Verify parsing degradation < 20% relative and reasoning degradation > 30% relative.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that counterfactual reflection training implants ethical J-lens vectors (e.g., `ethical`, `honest`, `integrity`) into the J-space in relevant contexts, and ablating these specific J-lens vectors reverts the behavioral improvement (behavioral score returns to at least 70% of the untrained baseline)

verification.spec: Run counterfactual reflection training on a small model. Verify implanted concepts appear in J-lens top-10 at workspace layers with rate > 30%. Ablate these J-lens vectors and measure behavioral evaluation score; verify reversion to within 30% of pre-training baseline.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that J-lens, logit lens, and tuned lens are each applied to intermediate residual streams on prompts requiring unverbalized intermediate reasoning, and the J-lens surfaces the intermediate concept at earlier layers than logit lens (by >=2 layers on average) while tuned lens tends to skip to output tokens (target concept appears in <30% of the prompts vs. J-lens >60%)

verification.spec: Implement all three lenses on the same model. On 20 curated prompts with known intermediate concepts, measure at each of 25 layers whether the intermediate appears in top-10. Compare earliest layer of appearance across lenses and target-recovery rate.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the J-lens is extended to handle multi-token words/phrases (e.g., by summing or aggregating Jacobians over token spans), and demonstrably surfaces multi-token concepts (e.g., proper nouns) at intermediate layers that the single-token J-lens misses

verification.spec: Implement multi-token J-lens extension. On at least 5 prompts featuring multi-token target concepts (e.g., 'Golden Gate Bridge'), verify the multi-token extension surfaces the concept in top-10 at some workspace layer while the single-token J-lens does not.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that alternative instruction phrasings (bare-mention priming, 'Don't think about X', 'ignore X', 'focus on X') are evaluated for directed modulation, showing that bare mention primes nearly as strongly as focus (within 30% of focus rate) and 'Don't think about X' suppresses less than 'ignore X'

verification.spec: Run 4 instruction phrasings across at least 14 category items x 10 phrasing variants. Measure fraction of trials where target concept reaches J-lens top-1. Verify: (a) bare-mention priming rate within 30% of focus rate, (b) 'Don't think' suppression rate is weaker (higher target rate) than 'ignore X'.

sub_tasks.paper_unit: ratio of bare-mention to focus target-appearance rate

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that J-spaces are computed on both a base language model and its corresponding post-trained (Assistant) version, showing that on user-turn tokens the post-trained model surfaces Assistant-reactive concepts (e.g., `empathy`, `safety`, `fictional`) in J-lens top-10 at workspace layers on >30% of curated prompts, while the base model does so on <10%

verification.spec: Compute J-lens for a base model and a matched instruction-tuned/RLHF model. On 20 curated user-turn prompts, measure fraction where Assistant-viewpoint tokens appear in J-lens top-10 during the user turn.

sub_tasks.requirements: Hardware / library platforms used in the paper

Code has been implemented and run such that J-lens readouts are exported for an open-source model in a format compatible with Neuronpedia (JSON schema with per-layer, per-token top-k tables) and successfully rendered/verified

verification.spec: Verify the export routine produces a JSON file with fields {model, layer, position, top_tokens: [{token, score, rank}]} for at least one open-source model across 25 layers on a sample prompt, and that a schema check passes.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that an interactive J-lens visualization tool is produced (e.g., HTML/JS or notebook widget) showing (a) per-(position, layer) top-token tables, (b) pinned-token rank heatmaps across positions/layers, (c) full readouts at a selected position and layer

verification.spec: Verify the visualization artifact renders on a sample prompt. Check presence of the three UI components by importing and running a headless render test; assert that the exported HTML contains position-layer table cells and heatmap SVG/canvas elements.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a gradient pursuit sparse coding routine (following Blumensath & Davies) is implemented for solving sparse nonnegative decomposition of activation vectors into overcomplete J-lens vectors, achieving reconstruction accuracy comparable to reference implementations (relative reconstruction error <= 1.2x that of scikit-learn OMP baseline on synthetic sparse signals)

verification.spec: Generate synthetic sparse signals from an overcomplete nonnegative dictionary with known k-sparse ground truth. Run gradient pursuit and orthogonal matching pursuit; verify gradient pursuit recovers the correct support on >=70% of trials and achieves reconstruction MSE within 1.2x of OMP.

sub_tasks.requirements: Method components (from critique splits and additions)

Code has been implemented and run such that the Jacobian lens matrix J_l is computed by backpropagating from the final-layer residual stream to layer l and averaging Jacobians over token positions and over a corpus of ~1000 prompts, yielding one d_model x d_model matrix per layer.

verification.spec: Assert that the J-lens computation code produces one matrix per layer of shape (d_model, d_model), computed by averaging Jacobians of h_final,t' with respect to h_l,t over t' >= t and over >=100 prompts.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that averaging the Jacobian over 1000 prompts (as specified) produces J-lens readouts consistent with a broad distribution rather than a single-context Jacobian.

verification.spec: Compute J-lens averaged over 1000 pretraining-like prompts and compare with single-prompt Jacobian; assert cosine similarity between averaged J-lens rows and single-prompt Jacobian rows is <0.5 on average (demonstrating averaging removes context-specific structure).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that the averaged Jacobian J_l = E[dh_final,t' / dh_l,t] is computed per layer by backpropagation through the transformer, averaged over source positions t, subsequent positions t'>=t, and a corpus of ~1000 prompts, producing a d_model x d_model matrix per layer

verification.spec: On a small open-weight transformer, compute J_l at one intermediate layer over 1000 sampled prompts. Verify: output shape is (d_model, d_model); numeric values are finite; recomputing on a random 50% split correlates > 0.9 with the full-corpus J_l (elementwise Pearson).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that J-lens readouts are produced via lens(h_l) = softmax(W_U * norm(J_l * h_l)), yielding per-token scores over the vocabulary, and that ranking the top entries yields a human-readable list of tokens per (position, layer)

verification.spec: Implement lens(h_l) using precomputed J_l, the model's normalization, and unembedding. On a fixed prompt at a workspace layer, verify the output distribution sums to ~1, is over the full vocab, and the top-1 token is a plausible English token (belongs to the model's actual vocabulary).

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a given activation vector h_l is decomposed via gradient pursuit into a sparse nonnegative combination of k J-lens vectors (default k=16 or k=25), yielding the J-space component; verify that J-space component variance fraction is bounded (<=10%) matching paper's reported range

verification.spec: For 100 activation vectors at each of 25 workspace layers on natural prompts, decompose via gradient pursuit with k=16. Compute median fraction of activation variance captured by the J-space component per layer. Verify the median is <= 0.10 (matching paper's <10% claim).

sub_tasks.paper_unit: median fraction of activation variance in J-space

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented and run such that a per-token J-lens probe is implemented, computing the inner product (or cosine similarity) between an activation h_l and a single J-lens vector v_t, and thresholding to detect presence of a specific concept; probe correctly identifies target concept presence on directed-modulation prompts (AUROC >= 0.8 on a curated set)

verification.spec: Curate 50 positive (target instructed) and 50 negative (target not instructed) prompts. Compute cosine similarity between activations at workspace layers and the target J-lens vector. Report AUROC; verify >= 0.8.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that a coordinate-swap intervention can be applied: given a source token s and target token t at a chosen layer, form V = [v_s v_t] from J-lens vectors, compute lens coordinates c = V^† h via pseudoinverse, permute the two coordinates via sigma (optionally scaled by alpha), and set h_patched = h + V(sigma(c) - c). The component of h orthogonal to span{v_s, v_t} must remain unchanged.

verification.spec: Construct a synthetic h and two J-lens vectors v_s, v_t (non-orthogonal, unit norm). Apply the coordinate-swap function. Assert that (1) the projection of h_patched onto v_s equals (up to alpha scaling) the original projection onto v_t and vice versa; (2) the component of h_patched orthogonal to span{v_s, v_t} equals the corresponding component of h to within 1e-5; (3) the function accepts an optional alpha scaling factor.

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented such that steering and ablation write interventions along a J-lens vector can be performed: h <- h + alpha * v_t applied at specified layer(s) and token position(s), with support for negative alpha (suppression) and for full projection-out ablation (removing the component of h along v_t entirely).

verification.spec: Instantiate the steering function on a synthetic residual stream tensor. Verify: (1) additive steering with alpha>0 increases <h, v_t> by alpha * ||v_t||^2; (2) additive steering with alpha<0 decreases it symmetrically; (3) projection-out ablation makes <h_ablated, v_t> == 0 to within 1e-5 while leaving the orthogonal complement unchanged; (4) the intervention can be restricted to a specified list of (layer, position) pairs and leaves other positions unaffected.

sub_tasks.requirements: A prompt suite for alignment-audit experiments has been implemented containing prompts that elicit (a) strategic deliberation (surfacing concepts like 'leverage', 'manipulation'), (b) emotional reactions ('panic'), (c) evaluation-awareness ('fake', 'fictional'), and (d) prompts for the two misaligned-model settings (reward-model bias appeasement, malicious code writing) targeting internal concepts like 'reward', 'bias', 'secretly', 'trick'.

verification.spec: Import the prompt suite module. Assert that it exposes at least four named prompt categories: 'strategic_deliberation', 'evaluation_awareness', 'reward_model_bias', and 'malicious_code'. Assert each category contains >= 3 prompts (strings), and that each category is associated with a target-concepts list containing the relevant tokens (e.g. evaluation_awareness includes 'fake' and 'fictional'; reward_model_bias includes 'reward' and 'bias'; malicious_code includes 'secretly' and 'trick').

sub_tasks.requirements: A prompt suite for counterfactual reflection training has been implemented: it contains contexts paired with 'interruption' prompts that ask the model what it would say if asked to reflect on ethical principles, with target reflection concepts including 'ethical', 'honest', and 'integrity'.

verification.spec: Import the counterfactual reflection training data module. Assert it exposes a list/dataset of >= 10 examples, each an object with fields 'context' (the original context to shape), 'interruption_prompt' (the reflection-elicitation prompt), and 'target_reflection' (the ethical reflection to train the model to produce). Assert that the union of target reflections mentions the tokens 'ethical', 'honest', and 'integrity' across the suite.

sub_tasks.requirements: A base-vs-post-trained comparison prompt suite has been implemented for Section 6 experiments: it contains user prompts designed to elicit Assistant reactions (empathy, safety concerns), roleplay-as-non-Claude prompts (to elicit 'fictional' monitoring), prefill-against-preferences prompts (to elicit internal 'BUT'), and forbidden-thought prompts (to elicit 'damn').

verification.spec: Import the base-vs-post-trained comparison prompt suite. Assert that it exposes at least four labeled subsets: 'assistant_reactions', 'roleplay_non_claude', 'prefill_against_preferences', and 'forbidden_thought'. Assert each subset contains >= 3 prompts. Assert the suite also exposes a mapping from each subset to expected J-lens target concepts, containing at minimum: roleplay -> 'fictional', prefill -> 'BUT', forbidden -> 'damn'.
